messages:
dario: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands infra update — can we clarify the eviction policy for Dedicated prewarm pools? Specifically: what's the exact eviction order (spot vs burst vs reserved), and will prewarmed nodes be drained for higher‑tier customers?

alex_infra: Short answer: current plan is spot -> burst -> reserved. Prewarm nodes are treated as 'reserved' unless explicitly marked preemptible. We're proposing an opt-in tag customers can set if they want cheaper, preemptible prewarm.

maya_product: How does that interact with autoscaler and regional fallbacks when supply dips? e.g., will requests auto-failover to another region or to a smaller model first?

alex_infra: Two-layer fallback: 1) model-family variant (quantized/smaller) within same region, 2) cross-region fallback if latency delta < regional_fallback_threshold_ms. We're adding a new config name 'regional_fallback_threshold_ms' and a customer-facing toggle.

julian_ml: From model side: prefer to fall back to quantized or 8-bit variants before crossing regions. That keeps latency predictable and avoids cross-region egress.

emily_support: We'll need a short support blurb explaining "possible model swap" vs "region reroute" so CS can set expectations. Can we also get guidance on how we annotate incidents when this happens?

alex_infra: Agree on both. Implementation notes: we'll use k8s node taints + autoscaler priorities for prewarm. Rough snippet: 
```
kubectl patch node <node> -p '{"spec":{"taints":[{"key":"prewarm","value":"true","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}'
```
And eviction flow will consult node labels: spot -> burst -> reserved. Prewarm flag toggles whether a reserved prewarm node is eligible for eviction.

dario: Pricing question — if a customer chooses to keep prewarmed buffer, are they billed differently?

maya_product: Proposal: add a 'prewarm-hourly' line item for Dedicated pools. Suggested pilot pricing = 50% of reserved hourly rate (covers capacity footprint + autoscaler overhead). Open to feedback.

alex_infra: Technical note: prewarm accounting will be via the capacity controller; billing event will include node-tags so we can surface it in invoices.

ops_bot: autoscaler: scale up 5 nodes in us-west-2 (prewarm) — reason: expected demand spike (scheduled job at 2026-03-23T15:00Z).

dario: OK — action items: Alex to draft eviction policy doc + config keys; Maya to draft pricing blurb and pilot plan; Emily to draft support copy and incident annotation template. Can we have first drafts by EOD Friday?

alex_infra: I'll open a PR with the policy doc by Friday EOD.

maya_product: Ack — will draft pricing pilot and send to finance for numbers.

emily_support: Ack — will prepare customer-facing copy and a short internal ops runbook.

dario: Thanks all :rocket:
